title: Affine normalization in the product of generic residue fields
statement:
Let $T$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] such that every quasi-compact open has finitely many irreducible components [def-weil-irreducible-components]. Write $
u_T:T^
u	o T$ for its componentwise normalization [def-weil-pbc-reduced-normalization]. For every affine open $U=\operatorname{Spec}A\subseteq T$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], let $I_U$ be the finite set of generic points of its irreducible components [def-sc-generic-point], set $C_U=\prod_{\eta\in I_U}\kappa_T(\eta)$ [def-weil-residue-field], and give $C_U$ the $A$-algebra structure obtained by taking germs and then residue classes. Let $D_U=\{c\in C_U:c	ext{ is integral over }A\}$ [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure]. There is a canonical isomorphism of $U$-schemes $
u_T^{-1}(U)\simeq\operatorname{Spec}D_U$, under which the normalization map is induced by $A	o D_U$. Moreover these identifications are compatible with affine open inclusions: for affine $W\subseteq U$, the generic points in $I_W$ identify with those in $I_U$ lying in $W$, their residue fields are unchanged, the projection $C_U	o C_W$ sends $D_U$ into $D_W$, and its restriction $D_U	o D_W$ is the restriction map on the sections of $
u_{T,*}\mathcal O_{T^
u}$. No reducedness, Noetherianity or finiteness of normalization is assumed. For $U=\varnothing$, both $C_U$ and $D_U$ are the zero ring and the inverse image is empty.

source.place: Tags 035P (lemma-description-normalization, parts (1)-(4)), 035O (lemma-normalization-reduced), 0CDV (lemma-normalization-in-terms-of-components); the restriction maps are those of the integral-closure sheaf in Definition 035H (definition-normalization-X-in-Y) and Lemma 035F (lemma-integral-closure).

proof.text: For an open $V\subseteq T$, the nonempty traces $Z\cap V$ of irreducible components $Z$ of $T$ are distinct irreducible components of $V$ by [lem-sc-components-open-injection]. Conversely, a component $H$ of $V$, regarded as an irreducible subset of $T$, is contained in a component $Z$ of $T$ by [lem-sc-irreducible-components-cover]. Then $H\subseteq Z\cap V$, so maximality gives equality. Each $Z$ has a unique generic point $\eta$ by [lem-sc-scheme-sober]. The equality $Z=\overline{\{\eta\}}$ shows that $Z\cap V\ne\varnothing$ exactly when $\eta\in V$, and then $\overline{\{\eta\}}^{\,V}=Z\cap V$. Thus the generic points of components of $V$ are exactly the generic points of $T$ belonging to $V$. Apply this to $U$ and to $W\subseteq U$ to obtain $I_W=I_U\cap W$. The set $I_U$ is finite by the hypothesis on quasi-compact opens.

source.place: Tags 004W (topology.tex, lemma-irreducible, (3)-(4)) and 01IS (schemes.tex, lemma-scheme-sober); applied to the components in Tag 0CDV.

proof.text: For $\eta\in I_U$, let $Z_\eta$ be the corresponding component of $T$ with its reduced induced structure. By [lem-weil-pbc-spec-irreducible-components-minimal-primes], its trace on $U=\operatorname{Spec}A$ is $V(\mathfrak p_\eta)$ for a minimal prime $\mathfrak p_\eta$ of $A$. The point $\mathfrak p_\eta$ is its generic point, since its closure consists precisely of the primes containing $\mathfrak p_\eta$. By [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme], the open $Z_\eta\cap U$ is therefore canonically $\operatorname{Spec}A_\eta$, where $A_\eta=A/\mathfrak p_\eta$, with structural map the quotient map from $A$. It is nonempty and integral. These identifications also apply to $Z_\eta\cap W$ whenever $\eta\in I_W$.

source.place: Tag 00ES (algebra.tex, lemma-irreducible, (3)); Tag 01J3 (schemes.tex, lemma-reduced-closed-subscheme), affine construction in its proof; Tag 0CDV.

proof.text:
Put $K_\eta=\kappa_T(\eta)$. The germ-compatible localization in [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-stalk-localization] identifies $\mathcal O_{T,\eta}$ with $A_{\mathfrak p_\eta}$. Its maximal ideal is $\mathfrak p_\eta A_{\mathfrak p_\eta}$: a fraction is a unit exactly when its numerator is outside $\mathfrak p_\eta$. The residue quotient [def-weil-residue-field] has the canonical isomorphism
$$A_{\mathfrak p_\eta}/\mathfrak p_\eta A_{\mathfrak p_\eta}\ \longrightarrow\ \operatorname{Frac}(A_\eta),\qquad [a/s]\longmapsto (a\bmod\mathfrak p_\eta)/(s\bmod\mathfrak p_\eta).$$
Its inverse sends a quotient of residue classes to $[a/s]$; cross multiplication proves both maps well-defined and inverse. By [lem-sc-integral-function-field-affine-fraction] for the integral scheme $Z_\eta$ and its nonempty affine open $Z_\eta\cap U$, this is its function field. Thus we canonically identify $k(Z_\eta)=K_\eta$, and $A\to A_\eta\to K_\eta$ is exactly the germ-then-residue map. This identification uses the generic germ, so it is independent of the chosen affine neighbourhood. For an affine inclusion $W\subseteq U$ containing $\eta$, the germ of a restricted section equals its original germ at $\eta$; taking the same residue quotient therefore makes these field identifications commute with restriction.

source.place: Tag 01HV (schemes.tex, lemma-spec-sheaves, (6)); Tag 01RV (morphisms.tex, lemma-integral-scheme-rational-functions) and Definition 01RW (definition-function-field); explicit residue-quotient calculation.

proof.text:
Let $B_\eta(U)\subseteq K_\eta$ be the integral closure of $A_\eta$ in this function field. Apply the affine clause of [def-fin-normalization-extension] to $Z_\eta$ and the degree-one extension $k(Z_\eta)/k(Z_\eta)$. It gives $
u_{Z_\eta}^{-1}(Z_\eta\cap U)=\operatorname{Spec}B_\eta(U)$, with map to $\operatorname{Spec}A_\eta$ induced by inclusion of $A_\eta$ in $B_\eta(U)$. By [def-weil-pbc-reduced-normalization], $T^
u$ is the coproduct of these component normalizations. Its summands form a disjoint open cover by [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-coproduct-family]. Restricting that cover to $
u_T^{-1}U$ gives
$$
u_T^{-1}U\simeq\coprod_{\eta\in I_U}\operatorname{Spec}B_\eta(U).$$
Components not meeting $U$ contribute the empty open. This argument uses neither reducedness of $T$ nor finiteness of any component normalization.

source.place: Tag 0CDV (lemma-normalization-in-terms-of-components); affine construction of Tags 035H and 035P, and the affine clause in blueprint def-fin-normalization-extension with L=K.

proof.text: Assume $U\ne\varnothing$, so $I_U\ne\varnothing$ by step 1; the empty case is checked in step 7. We identify $D_U$ with $\prod_{\eta\in I_U}B_\eta(U)$ inside $C_U$. A tuple integral over $A$ projects to elements integral over $A_\eta$, by projecting its monic equation and reducing the coefficients. Conversely, for a tuple $(b_\eta)$ with $b_\eta\in B_\eta(U)$, choose a monic equation over $A_\eta$ for each $b_\eta$. Lift its coefficients along the surjection $A\to A_\eta$, retaining leading coefficient $1$, to obtain a monic $P_\eta\in A[X]$ that kills $b_\eta$ in $K_\eta$. The finite product $P=\prod_\eta P_\eta$ is monic and kills the entire tuple: in coordinate $\eta$ its factor $P_\eta(b_\eta)$ vanishes. This proves equality using the monic-equation definition [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-affine-coproduct-spectrum] to step 4 to obtain the canonical isomorphism with $\operatorname{Spec}D_U$. Its structural map sends $a\in A$ to its images in each $B_\eta(U)\subseteq K_\eta$, hence is the specified $A\to D_U$.

source.place: Tag 035P (lemma-description-normalization, (3)-(4)); its finite-product integral-closure argument written with lifted monic polynomials; Tag 0CDV.

proof.text: Let $W\subseteq U$ be affine. Step 1 gives $I_W\subseteq I_U$; surviving points have the same ambient stalks and residue fields. On a surviving component, [def-sc-normalization] constructs the normalization algebra as a subsheaf of the constant sheaf $K_\eta$. On any nonempty irreducible open its sections in that constant sheaf are $K_\eta$: a locally constant function is constant since any two nonempty opens intersect. Restrictions in this ambient sheaf are identities. The affine charts of [def-fin-normalization-extension] are glued using these inclusions. Concretely, on a principal open $D(h)\subseteq Z_\eta\cap U$ with $h\ne0$, [lem-weil-pbc-integral-closure-commutes-localization] identifies its normalization ring with $B_\eta(U)_h\subseteq K_\eta$; its map sends $b/h^m$ to that same quotient in $K_\eta$. Thus the chart maps to the constant sheaf agree on a principal-open basis, hence on all opens by the sheaf axiom. Applying the affine chart description also to $Z_\eta\cap W$ identifies restriction with $B_\eta(U)\hookrightarrow B_\eta(W)$ inside $K_\eta$. Explicitly, if $c=(c_\eta)\in D_U$ satisfies $c^n+\sum_{j<n}a_jc^j=0$, then for every surviving $\eta\in I_W$ its unchanged coordinate satisfies $c_\eta^n+\sum_{j<n}(a_j|_W)c_\eta^j=0$ in $K_\eta$, because restriction preserves generic germs by step 3. Thus the projected tuple lies in $D_W$ by [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure]. No localization description of the arbitrary affine inclusion $W\subseteq U$ is needed.

source.place: Tags 035F (lemma-integral-closure), 035H (definition-normalization-X-in-Y), and 0307 (algebra.tex, lemma-integral-closure-localize): restrictions of the integral-closure algebra, first on principal opens and then by the sheaf axiom.

proof.text:
The summands in step 4 are disjoint open subsets. The sheaf gluing axiom therefore identifies sections on their union with the product of their section rings: tuples have no compatibility condition on disjoint intersections. Under these product identifications, restricting from $
u_T^{-1}U$ to $
u_T^{-1}W$ discards the summands not meeting $W$ and applies the maps of step 6 on the others. After the inclusions in the fields, this is exactly the projection $C_U	o C_W$. Its restriction $D_U	o D_W$ is therefore the restriction map of $
u_{T,*}\mathcal O_{T^
u}$, and the Spec identifications commute with the affine open inclusions. All identifications were specified by germs, subrings and the canonical coproduct-to-product-spectrum map, so they are canonical. If $U=\varnothing$, $I_U=\varnothing$, the product is the zero ring, its integral-closure subring is the zero ring (its sole element satisfies the monic polynomial $X$), and the coproduct and inverse image are empty. The same argument covers $W=\varnothing$.
